text:
Sam: Repro'd a persistent RSS increase on staging with our long-stream tool loop. 10k tokens over ~90s per session; after 3 sessions RSS up ~1.1GB and doesn't go down after sessions close.
Anya: steps + commit?
Sam: repro command: `tools/stream-sim --model redwood-v2-small --turns 40 --tool-loop 8 --stream=true --session-duration 90s` on commit 9f2c4a7. Happens reliably.
Lee: can you share any allocator/profiling output?
Sam: quick tail of jemalloc + pprof summary pasted: 
```
# jemalloc stats (end): allocated: 6.7G active: 7.9G mapped: 8.5G
# pprof heap -> top locations
kv_cache.cpp:reserve_slot 31%
slab_alloc 18%
request_pool.cpp:alloc 12%
Live refs: long_kv_entries 45% of objects pinned
```
Anya: reserve_slot being the top one is suspicious. reserve is called on pagewalks during streaming, right?
Sam: yes. Streaming path hits prefix/KV a lot. My working hypothesis: reserve creates entries that should be transient but remain resident due to stale index refs.
Dario: do we have counters for ghost refs / weak refs? We added weak refs in March to allow eviction.
Sam: weak_ref_count looks normal. But allocator logs show "ghost_ref" increments that don't correspond to active sessions.
Morgan: slab fragmentation could also make memory appear to grow; lots of small allocations inside slabs block freeing.
Lee: can we run an allocation trace with profiling enabled and diff pmap before/after session close?
Sam: I did `malloc_conf:prof:true,lg_prof_sample:19` and compared runs. Samples show steady allocations from `kv_metadata::make_entry` even after sessions end. Index->page mapping seems to point to non-resident pages.
Anya: any recent change touching eviction?
Dario: yes — commit 9f2 introduced deferred index clearing to avoid stalls on eviction: we now push an index_clear task to a BG queue instead of clearing inline.
Sam: I toggled deferred vs immediate index clear in my repro. Immediate clear => memory drops back to baseline after session. Deferred => leak reproduces. Strong correlation.
Lee: sounds like a race: deferred clear runs after a re-insert and ends up leaving a dangling pointer or duplicate ref.
Morgan: we should instrument index insert/clear with counters and asserts. Also add an index_ref_count per page metric.
Sam: quick patch I tried: replace naive deferred clear with CAS semantics: `if (index.ptr == old_page) atomic_compare_exchange_strong(&index.ptr, &old_page, nullptr)` — ran harness, memory stabilized.
Anya: ok that's a good band-aid. We need a proper fix in the eviction flow: ensure clear only removes the same page we thought we freed, and avoid re-insert races.
Dario: I'll add a deterministic integration test that exercises eviction concurrently with reader re-inserts. We should run it 1000 iterations and assert no net RSS growth.
Lee: also run TSAN on index ops to catch ordering bugs. I'll queue a TSAN job for the merge candidate.
Morgan: ops: can we add a nightly longstream job (30m) to catch regressions earlier? Short CI loops miss these races.
Anya: yes, I'll add `infra-schedules/longstream-nightly` and wire an alert to eng-runtime-oncall if RSS growth > 500MB over baseline. Also expose `kv.evictions.pending` and `kv.index.pending_clears` in the console.
Sam: PR up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4321 — CAS check + unit test + alloc-profiling script. CI running.
ci-bot: Job queued: integration-longstream (30m) — will report back.
Lee: flamegraph of the fixed run shows reserve_slot still a top allocator but live residency collapses after session close.
Dario: action items:
- Sam: track PR and follow CI, collect heap profiles on CI run
- Dario: add the eviction/race integration test + run 1000 iterations locally
- Lee: TSAN run on branch and review index ops ordering
- Morgan: schedule nightly longstream job and add alert thresholds
- Anya: expose deferred queue length & pending clears metric to Console, add playbook entry
Sam: thanks — I'll keep monitoring staging. If CI heap snapshots look good I'll roll the fix to canary. :eyes:
Anya: good work catching the deferred-clear regression.
Sam: learned to be suspicious of background-clears when memory doesn't drop.
Lee: small follow-up: after merge let's add a short postmortem note in #postmortems with repro steps and perf graphs so we can correlate future regressions.
Sam: ok will write a short note.
Morgan: and maybe a perf dashboard panel showing longstream RSS over time per commit.
Sam: agreed. I'll seed one in Console. :thumbsup:
